topRisks.title: No CI pipeline builds and tests changes automatically
No authorization on sensitive actions: anonymous POST /reset deletes data and anonymous /about?show-details=true returns configuration
No CI workflow runs the test suite on every change
No server-side authentication: pipeline has no UseAuthentication/AddAuthentication and the destructive reset endpoint is explicitly [AllowAnonymous]
Checked-in OpenAPI spec is out of sync with the implemented routes and DTOs

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: TestingRepository.ResetTestingAsync is a ~75-line method mixing config lookup, connection, transaction and error handling (maintainability)

evidence.excerpt: public async Task<RetrieveResponse<int>> ResetTestingAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

findings.recommendation: Extract data-source resolution, connection/transaction execution and error logging into small private methods (or a shared unit-of-work helper) so the method has one purpose.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Duplicated blocks: same data-source-type switch repeated 3x and duplicated ProblemDetails/response blocks in middleware (maintainability)

evidence.excerpt: return dataSourceType.ToLowerInvariant() switch { "sqlserver" => ..., "postgresql" => ..., _ => throw new ConfigurationException(...) }
var problemDetails = new ProblemDetails { Status = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError, Title = "Internal Server Error", ...

findings.recommendation: Introduce a per-provider strategy/factory (connection string, connection, reset script) and a private WriteProblemAsync helper in the middleware.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: SystemController.About embeds application-metadata and display-name logic instead of delegating to a service
findings.standard: Azure Architecture Center - Cloud Design Patterns
findings.recommendation: Move the construction of AboutResponse into a service in the Services layer (like TestingController does) and keep the controller to HTTP mapping.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Shared project is a grab-bag (API middleware, logging, OpenTelemetry, OpenAPI, Swagger, configuration, exceptions) with low cohesion
findings.recommendation: Split Shared into cohesive projects (e.g. Web infrastructure vs. core configuration/exceptions) so the Domain/Repositories layers don't depend on ASP.NET-heavy code.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Inconsistent naming: folders/projects spelled 'PilotUtiltyApi' vs namespaces 'PilotUtilityApi'; AboutResponse sits in Models/Responses but uses the Models.Dto namespace
findings.recommendation: Fix the 'Utilty' typo in folder/project paths and align namespaces with folder structure (Responses vs Dto).

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Copy-pasted, incorrect XML doc on HealthCheck (describes a category table DTO list)

evidence.excerpt: A read only list of all DTO objects from the category table, or null if no objects exist.

findings.recommendation: Correct the <returns> text to state it returns 200 OK with "OK"; review other docs for copy/paste drift (e.g. ApiWebApplication example).

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: BuildServiceProvider() called during service registration creates a second container (ASP.NET Core analyzer ASP0000)
findings.recommendation: Pass the already-bound configuration or use AddOptions/IConfigureOptions (or the app-level instance) instead of building a provider mid-registration, which duplicates singletons.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: IDbConnection/IDbTransaction are not wrapped in using; connection leaks if BeginTransaction or Open throws

evidence.excerpt: var connection = CreateConnection(...); ... var transaction = connection.BeginTransaction();

findings.recommendation: Use 'using var connection' and 'using var transaction' (and OpenAsync) so disposal occurs on every path.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Nullable warnings suppressed with #pragma instead of addressed (non-nullable properties left uninitialized)

evidence.excerpt: #pragma warning disable CS8618 // Non-nullable field must contain a non-null value

findings.recommendation: Mark the properties 'required' or give them defaults/nullable types, and remove the pragma.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No CI pipeline builds and tests changes automatically

evidence.excerpt: ## Pull Request Process ... 5. You may merge the Pull Request in once you have the sign-off of two other developers

findings.recommendation: Add a CI workflow (e.g. .github/workflows/ci.yml) that runs dotnet restore/build/test on every push and pull request, and make it a required status check before merge.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No documented release process (tagging, changelog, publish)

evidence.excerpt: 4. Increase the version numbers in any examples files and the README.md ... The versioning scheme we use is SemVer

findings.recommendation: Document how releases are cut (version bump in Directory.Build.props, git tag, release notes, publish/deploy step) and automate it with a release workflow.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: Branching model not documented; review rule not demonstrably enforced

evidence.excerpt: 5. You may merge the Pull Request in once you have the sign-off of two other developers

findings.recommendation: Document the branching model (e.g. trunk-based with short-lived feature branches) and enforce it via branch protection with required reviews and status checks on main.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No automated dependency update configuration

evidence.excerpt: 1. Ensure any install or build dependencies are removed before the end of the layer when doing a build.

findings.recommendation: Add .github/dependabot.yml (nuget ecosystem) or Renovate config, or document a scheduled dependency review cadence.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting process

evidence.excerpt: reported by contacting the project team at ... (Code of Conduct contact only; no security reporting path)

findings.recommendation: Add a SECURITY.md describing supported versions and how to privately report vulnerabilities.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No CHANGELOG or release notes maintained

evidence.excerpt: Update the README.md with details of changes ... Increase the version numbers (no changelog step)

findings.recommendation: Add a CHANGELOG.md (e.g. Keep a Changelog format) and require an entry per pull request or release.

findings.subject: Twelve-Factor App
findings.title: App manages its own rolling log files in addition to writing to stdout
findings.recommendation: Make stdout (Console sink, ideally CompactJsonFormatter) the only default sink and leave routing/retention to the execution environment or the OTLP pipeline. Keep the File sink only as a Development-only override.

findings.subject: API Design
findings.title: Checked-in OpenAPI spec is out of sync with the implemented routes and DTOs
findings.recommendation: Regenerate docs/PilotUtilityApi_v1.json from the running app (or in CI) and fail the build on drift. The current file omits the v1 path prefix, the required flag on show-details, the AboutResponse.applicationConfiguration property, and the configured info title, version and contact.

findings.subject: API Design
findings.title: Inconsistent URL versioning and an RPC-style action route

evidence.excerpt: ApiVersionReader.Combine(new HeaderApiVersionReader("api-version"), new QueryStringApiVersionReader(), new UrlSegmentApiVersionReader())

findings.standard: Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines - URL structure / versioning
findings.recommendation: Choose one versioning mechanism, and a single URL convention for all endpoints. Model reset as a resource or a documented custom action (e.g. POST /v1/testing:reset) instead of an ad-hoc verb route. Alternatively, document the system endpoints as deliberately unversioned.

findings.subject: API Design
findings.title: Reset endpoint returns an empty 400 with the error in a Warning header, and has an inconsistent success shape

evidence.excerpt: Response.Headers.Append("Warning", response.ErrorMessage ?? "An error occurred"); return BadRequest();
if (response.Result == null || response.Result == 0) { return NoContent(); } ... return Ok(response.Result);

findings.standard: Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines - HTTP status codes / error response
findings.recommendation: Return a structured error body (ProblemDetails or the Azure error object) with a status that matches the failure, such as 500 for service or database faults and 4xx only for client errors. Do not put the error message in the Warning header. Use one consistent success shape, e.g. 200 with a JSON object holding the count.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: No server-side authentication: pipeline has no UseAuthentication/AddAuthentication and the destructive reset endpoint is explicitly [AllowAnonymous]
findings.recommendation: Register authentication (e.g. JWT bearer/OIDC via a vetted IdP), call UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization, and apply a fallback policy requiring authenticated users; allow anonymous only on healthcheck.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: No authorization on sensitive actions: anonymous POST /reset deletes data and anonymous /about?show-details=true returns configuration
findings.recommendation: Protect reset with [Authorize] using a role/policy (and disable it outside test environments); require authorization for /about show-details, keeping only /healthcheck anonymous.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: Implicit network trust: all endpoints anonymous and AllowedHosts is wildcard; no explicit verification of callers
findings.standard: OWASP Zero Trust Architecture Cheat Sheet
findings.recommendation: Verify every caller explicitly (token + scoped policies), restrict AllowedHosts to known hostnames, and use least-privilege database credentials.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: HTTPS redirection is enabled only in Development; no HSTS; HTTP-only launch URL
findings.recommendation: Call UseHttpsRedirection() (and UseHsts()) in all environments, or document and verify that TLS is terminated and HTTP is rejected at the ingress; add an https:// applicationUrl to launchSettings.

findings.subject: Testing
findings.title: Placeholder and weak-assertion tests do not verify real behavior
findings.recommendation: Replace the Assert.Pass placeholder with real Domain tests or remove it. In the 'default warning' controller test, set up the scenario its name describes and assert the Warning header value.

findings.subject: Testing
findings.title: No CI workflow runs the test suite on every change

evidence.excerpt: Tests are run manually ("Run the relevant test projects"); no .github/workflows CI files exist in the target.

findings.recommendation: Add a CI workflow that runs 'dotnet test' (with coverlet collection) on every push and pull request, and make it a required check.

findings.subject: Observability
findings.title: Error correlation ID is an ad-hoc GUID, not tied to the trace ID or logged as a structured property
findings.recommendation: Use Activity.Current?.TraceId as the correlation ID (or push it and any inbound X-Correlation-ID into Serilog LogContext as a separate CorrelationId property) so it is searchable and links logs to traces. Also return it for the UserException path.

findings.subject: Observability
findings.title: No SLOs or SLIs documented

evidence.excerpt: README and docs/ contain no availability/latency objectives or indicators

findings.recommendation: Document at least SLIs (e.g. request success rate, p95 latency from http.server.request.duration) and target SLOs in the README or docs/.

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: No NuGet lock file; restore is not locked to exact transitive versions

evidence.excerpt: <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally> (no RestorePackagesWithLockFile; no packages.lock.json at repo root)
PropertyGroup sets Version/TargetFramework/Nullable only; RestorePackagesWithLockFile not set

findings.standard: NuGet package restore with lock file (fallback rubric: best-practice gap)
findings.recommendation: Set <RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile> in Directory.Build.props, commit the generated packages.lock.json files, and use --locked-mode in CI.

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: No SBOM or license inventory present

evidence.excerpt: <ItemGroup> of PackageVersion entries; no sbom.json / *.cdx.json / *.spdx.json found at repo root

findings.recommendation: Generate a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM in CI (e.g. CycloneDX for .NET) and publish it as a build artifact or commit it.

findings.subject: Operations
findings.title: No retry with backoff for transient database failures
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded retry with exponential backoff and jitter for transient connection errors (e.g. Polly/Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience, or provider retry options such as EnableRetryOnFailure/Npgsql retry).
